body: C2 under A3 (W4). Trigger: a test sprint builds a time control control--foo for scenario X (waits "control: control--foo"); tests stamp keeps waits on every scenario (scripts/tests:cmd_stamp l.3186 "for name in ("part", "class", "harm", "waits")", and for a keep, kept = dict(old[...]) carries it forward forever). On the next /plan-tests, X's story is untouched, so assembled_plan adds X as a standing keep copied from the stamp, waits included (l.1276 recorded = {... if name != "issue"}). No planner records a controls item for control--foo, because the product already carries it. Path: SKILL step 8 -> tests plan -> scripts/tests:assembled_plan -> plan_failures -> control_failures l.1169: "elif (waited_control(scenario) or \"\").startswith(CONTROL_PREFIX) and waited_control(scenario) not in ids:" fires for every action, keep included, so assembly refuses "scenario X: it waits on time control control--foo, which no time control item records". The scenario is no planner's item (origins has no entry), so no fix under step 6's "Fixing a planner's items" applies, and every later plan fails to assemble while the stamp records that waits. Harm: /plan-tests cannot produce a plan once any earlier test sprint built a time control and its waiting scenario stands. The sprint's call limits the control:control--<slug> rule to a planned new or rewrite ("A planned new or rewrite names waits ... A control: control--<slug> value must name a control item in the plan"). Scope: caused (control_failures and the waits stamp are new in this change).

body: C2 under A3 (and A9). Entry: tests run [--sprint] (a script for developers and operators the review facts list) -> cmd_run -> suite_outcome -> run_suite -> read_stream. read_stream's loop runs only while the suite's stdout pipe is open (scripts/tests:1839 'while output is not None:'), and ends it on stdout EOF (l.1849-1851 'output = output if data else None'), not on the suite command's exit or on every planned result landing. Trigger A: the suite command's process closes or replaces the inherited stdout, as a wrapper that starts with 'exec > run.log 2>&1' or a testing.run that ends in '> /dev/null 2>&1' does under sh's exec of a single command. stdout reads EOF at once, the loop ends, and the tool then sits in proc.wait(timeout=max(silence - (now - last), 0)) (l.1853-1856) without reading the FIFO: results that land meanwhile reset no clock, and once the pipe buffer fills the writers block. Any suite that runs longer than testing.silence in total is stopped as 'silence', its process group killed (stop_suite), and every test whose line had not yet been read fails with 'the suite command reported no result; the run stopped after testing.silence seconds with no result' (unreported, l.1897-1904) though results were arriving the whole time. Trigger B (the reverse): the suite command exits but leaves a process that inherited stdout, such as a test stack or server it started in the background. The loop waits the full silence period after the last result, then records stopped='silence' over a round in which every test reported, and cmd_run and round_rows print 'the run stopped: no result arrived for testing.silence' (l.2146-2147, l.2965), which is false, and every round wastes testing.silence seconds. Harm: a correctly configured suite command gets a wrong verdict (tests failed that passed) and a false stop report, and the sprint's loop files fix tasks for tests that never failed. Scope: caused; read_stream and run_suite are new in this change (W2).

C1, W5 (and the I-less W5 call: 'On accept, the verifier sends each named test back (W1 path)'). Entry: test sprint step 6 -> tests run --sprint (a round whose testing.leftovers count grew) -> tests failures lists leftovers--<kind> -> tests tasks --stage fix (stage_fix) -> fixer records change=none with tests=[<scenario>] -> verify task -> core.md {{TEST-VERIFY-PROMPT}} 'A grown leftover count': 'On accepting it, send each test it names back to a test task: tasks item set <that scenario's latest item in the tests pool> --state sent-back'. Where it ends: when the named scenario's test was not written in this test sprint (action keep, or adopt from a legacy suite), no test task ran for it, so the tests pool holds no item for it and the verifier has nothing to send back. sent_back_tests/refiled_tests (scripts/tests:2341-2377) refile only from a tests item in state sent-back, and stage_write files a test task only for actions in WRITTEN (new, rewrite, retire; l.2558-2559), so no test task is ever filed for that scenario. unrewritten_tests (l.2978-2993) then requires 'a test task with key <named> closed done after the accepting verify task' and complete_failures appends 'fixes item ..., accepted, names test <sid> as leaving the resource behind, and no test task rewrote it' on every call: TESTS COMPLETE can never print, and the gate round grows the same count again, so step 6 (no cap) refiles the same leftovers fix. Outcome not reached: W5's 'a count that grew fails the round' has no route to a passing run when a kept or adopted test leaks, which is the likeliest leaker since no earlier sprint measured leftovers. The W1 fix-verifier path ('send the test back too: tasks item set <that scenario's latest item in the tests pool>') fails through the same site for a kept or adopted test, so that test is never rewritten. Scope: caused; the leftovers path, unrewritten_tests, and the send-back text are new in this change.

Where it ends: discover:165 `budget = (config.get("hunt") or {}).get("area_lines") or 2500` gives the review config's hunt.area_lines a code default of 2500, though review::load_hunt (review:641) already requires hunt.area_lines and refuses where it is missing. Outcome: W9 'Every setting in the suite's own scripts ... moves to the project's configuration with no default in code, and a tool that finds one missing refuses and names the key' (decision settings-have-no-code-defaults: 'Code that finds a setting missing refuses to start and names the missing key'). The W9 sweep missed this site, so a review config without hunt.area_lines cuts discovery areas at 2500 lines and names nothing. Second failure at the same owner frame: W9's notes say 'Each tool's owner frame adds tasks.Unset to the refusals it already catches'. cmd_areas reaches review.scoped_files -> tree_files -> project_folders -> declared_folders, which now raises review.issues.tasks.Unset where .ok-planner/config.json is missing or sets no folders (it returned [] at the base). discover::main (discover:799) catches only (InputError, review.ReviewError), so the Unset falls to the outer catch-all and ends as a DISCOVER.RUN.FAILED event with a trace, not the 'discover: ... sets no folders; run /ok, which writes it' refusal that every sibling tool (review, tests, ports, stack, run-group, docker-sweep, dashboard, surface-corpus) prints. Scope: the 2500 default stood the same at the base, and W9's outcome fails through it. The Unset path is caused by the change to review::declared_folders.

Entry point: the edit hook, scripts/hooks/post-edit.js:57-58, calls plumbline's findProjectRoot and then inProject(root, target). findProjectRoot (plumbline:733-740) also calls inProject for a file that has no .ok-planner ancestor. inProject (plumbline:686-690) asks declaredFolders (plumbline:677-684) for the folders the project owns outside its root. Where it ends: declaredFolders still defaults the setting. `if (!fs.existsSync(configPath)) return [];` and `if (read.userConfig === null || !('folders' in read.userConfig)) return [];` read a missing .ok-planner/config.json, or one that sets no folders, as 'the estate root alone'. They do not refuse and name the key. Outcome: W9 says 'a tool that finds one missing refuses and names the key'. The amended decision project-declares-its-folders says the list has 'no default', and 'Every tool that lists or scopes the project's code reads that list: ... the lint and its edit hook'. W9 removed this default from loadConfig (unsetLintKeys) and from review::declared_folders, but it left it in the lint's other folders reader. Trigger: a project whose config is missing or sets no folders, and an edit to a file in a folder the project owns beside its root. Old and new outcome: inProject returns false, so the hook lints nothing and prints nothing. The edit goes unlinted, and no message names the missing folders key. An edit inside the root does print loadConfig's refusal. Scope: the code stood the same at the base, where the decision still gave folders its 'root alone' default. W9's outcome fails through it.

body: B7 (rewrite; B2 rewrite across Trued-up projects). User left behind: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review::declared_folders, in the release, and through review::project_folders every tool that lists the project's folders (review changed/areas/checks/snapshot/certified, tests window/groups/plan/run/stray/complete, docs window). Its goal, from decision project-declares-its-folders, story project-spans-folders, and W9's own call ('the review's use of config-check for folders, which must not switch to root alone because an unrelated key is absent'): read the declared folders unless folders itself is malformed. Before: scripts/plumbline::testingDefects accepted the one-test form ('run' with {path}, 'timeout'), so config-check exited 0 and declared_folders returned config.folders. After: testingDefects returns ['testing declares the earlier one-test form; run /ok, ...'] (plumbline:353), config-check exits 2, and declared_folders (review:193-195) returns [] with the note 'is malformed, so the review reads the project root alone'. Trigger: a multi-folder project whose config declares the earlier testing form, trued up to this release, in the window before the owner answers true-up's testing:.ok-planner/config.json input question (true-up's plan writes the new vendored lint and review first; testing_question also waits while any other config defect stands, true-up:2851). Outcome: review changed and sprint certification drop every changed file under the declared folders, and /converge areas skip them, while the B2 ruling only accepts that bin/tests and config-check refuse the earlier form. Scope: caused (the change turned a config that passed config-check into one that fails it; declared_folders' all-defects test stood at the base).

C2 under A3 (an operator script gives a wrong result; also A9: the round reports failures that did not happen). Trigger: a suite command whose own stdout leaves the tool's pipe before the suite ends, such as testing.run = 'node scripts/suite.mjs {tests} {results} > suite.log' (the shell execs the single command with its redirect, so the pipe's write end closes at once), or a runner that daemonizes its workers. Path: cmd_run -> suite_outcome -> run_suite -> read_stream. read_stream's select loop runs only 'while output is not None' (tests:1839) and sets output = None on the pipe's EOF (tests:1851); it then calls proc.wait(timeout=max(silence - (time.monotonic() - last), 0)) (tests:1854) without reading the FIFO, so results that land during that wait never refresh 'last', and once the FIFO's pipe buffer (64 KiB, about 128 lines of 512 bytes) fills, every worker blocks on its write. Harm: any suite that runs longer than testing.silence after its stdout closed is stopped with stopped='silence' (tests:1856), the stop kills the group, and every test not yet read is recorded failed with 'the run stopped after testing.silence seconds with no result', though results kept arriving; the W2 outcome is a stop after silence seconds with no result. The fix loop then files fix tasks for passing tests, and tests complete cannot pass. Scope: caused (new code, B4).

C2 under A1 (and A8: plumbline-coding rule 3.2, a check-then-write with no lock). Trigger: two recorded runs on one test sprint at once, such as two sessions each running 'tests run --sprint <path>' (or one with --failing). Path: cmd_run computes number = len(results_rounds(root, sprint)) + 1 (tests:2116) from a plain read, then appends a header, result lines as they land, and a closing line over the whole run (tests:2122-2130), holding no lock. Both runs take the same number and interleave their lines. results_rounds then resets rounds[number] at the second header (tests:1949-1951), dropping the first run's planned list and tasks_closed, keeps whichever result line per scenario landed first from either run (tests:1955), and takes the closing line of whichever closed last. Harm: the -results.jsonl record holds a round no complete run produced, and tests failures, stage_fix, complete_failures, and cmd_stamp read it as the latest round. At the base, each round was one line written once, so two concurrent rounds stayed two whole records. Scope: caused (B5's streamed record).

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests::cmd_report, cmd_ports, complete_failures (through ported_items). Before: every item in the ports pool was listed, added to checks, and required in checks. After: only items recorded by the latest legacy task of each key. Users: the completion report's reader (sees the checks actually ported, not a refused attempt's), test sprint step 5 (tests ports adds the revised command after a refile, W23), and tests complete (no longer demands a superseded command in checks). Each goal holds: a superseded item names a check the run no longer ports.

body: Reviewed the declare-to-write chain: /plan-sprint section 5 Docspecs and the DOCSPEC-DEFINITION/TEMPLATE (artifact-definitions.md:162-234) let the owner declare a docspec's ## Notes, 'the owner's standing instructions to the writer: an outline, a passage to keep verbatim, a thing to leave out' (artifact-definitions.md:176). In /plan-docs, the planner and the writer act only through DOC-EDIT-RULES (plan-docs/core.md:7-26), whose rules fire on false claims, listed elements, closed sprints, ## Shape/layout (line 19), and ## Reader/## Covers (line 20); no rule fires on a departure from ## Notes, and line 23 says 'Every other sentence stays as written.' The writer prompt reads ## Notes (line 213) but may edit only where a rule fires. So when the owner adds or amends a Notes instruction on a docspec with existing files (e.g. Notes: 'Keep the sentence "This tool is in beta." verbatim at the top of each file'), docs window reaches the docspec for its own text change, the planner finds no rule that fires on any file, the docspec gets 'No item: nothing its reader sees changed.' (plan-docs/SKILL.md section 5), and the stamp moves forward with the instruction never applied; the same holds for a file that is a change item for another reason. The story promises: 'a way to declare each kind of documentation my project keeps ... so that whoever writes that documentation writes what I asked for'; decision docspec-stamp-opens-the-window takes a docspec 'whose own text ... changed since its stamp'. Saw: only newly written files honor Notes; existing documentation never gets the owner's Notes instructions. Evidence: plan-docs/core.md:19-23 (the rules table and 'Every other sentence stays as written.'); artifact-definitions.md:176.

Reviewed the style pass, DOC-STYLE-PROMPT (plan-docs/core.md:277-337). It reads the docspec whole, then 'revise it against the docspec's ## Shape and layout, the worked example, and the writing standard' (line 314), and its limit is only 'keep every claim's meaning, add no claim, and cut none' (line 323). It is never told to keep what the docspec's ## Notes orders, so a passage the owner's Notes says to keep verbatim (artifact-definitions.md:176: 'a passage to keep verbatim') may be reworded by the style pass under the writing standard (shortest word, active voice), and an outline Notes gives may be reordered to the worked example's order. The story promises: 'so that whoever writes that documentation writes what I asked for'. Saw: the cold style pass, which edits every reviewed file, takes the shape, example, and standard as its only authorities and can undo the Notes instructions the writer followed. Evidence: plan-docs/core.md:314-325.

body: Reviewed skill:converge sprint mode against the completion contract and review certified. SKILL.md (Loop 2, closing paragraph) says: "In sprint mode, when the loop ends, run the checks once more ... A file that fails now becomes a stuck defect with the check's output, and the loop does not reopen." It gives no command and no fields for that defect, unlike step 3 of sprint mode, which files reports with --field site=<the file> --field 'files=["<the file>"]'. review certified (scripts/review::check_failures via stuck_files) allows a failing check only on a file a stuck defect lists in its files or site field. The story promises: a way to know whether what I approved was delivered, so that done means the same thing for every sprint; the contract's item 2 says the checks pass "or fail only where sprint certification's return lists the failure as a stuck defect", and the goal rule says such a stuck defect holds no term open. Saw, in a scratch project (stack run certify-completion-8ff92de6): a stuck defect filed with only the check's output as its body (tasks item add --pool defects --key gate --state stuck --body "node .ok-planner/bin/plumbline src/late.py: comment-hygiene violation at line 1" -> i2), listed in the return block as "stuck i2: final checks failed on src/late.py"; review certified printed: "item 2 (checks): fails" / "SPRINT NOT COMPLETE" / "- node .ok-planner/bin/plumbline fails on src/late.py, which no stuck defect lists", exit 2. The same tree state with files set on the stuck defect prints SPRINT COMPLETE (verified with stuck i1 site=src/app.py: "item 2 (checks): holds"). So the verdict depends on how a session improvises the unspecified defect, and a sprint the contract calls done is reported not complete.

One gap: a defect issue the backlog takes up whose report the merge rejects for any reason but 'gone' or 'left alone' (merge.md step 2: 'A report whose harm no entry covers is rejected, with the list's reason'; step 1: 'A report whose code does not do what the report says is rejected') is never settled. owner-list.md reads 'the rejected reports with an issue field' but its 'Close the issues the run resolved' section closes only two kinds: 'For every report with an issue field that the merge rejected as gone, close its issue as answered' and 'For every report with an issue field that the merge rejected as left alone, close its issue the same way'. A report rejected as not covered by the accept list gets no close, no revise, and no route, so its issue stays open at route defect; triage skips it as already routed, and every later drive, analysis, or defects run takes it up again through review backlog (BACKLOG_STATES = open, verified), rejects it again, and shows it again as a rejected-report row in the calls table for the owner's veto. The story promises: 'found and fixed without me, so that I meet only the questions that need my judgment'; the cheatsheet's Defect issues section says a defect the run found not real or left standing by the accept list 'closes its issue as answered' with the reason; decision defects-outside-scope-become-defect-issues says a defect issue 'asks the owner for no judgment'. body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:cmd_run. What the code does: a recorded run reads the round number from a plain read, number = len(results_rounds(root, sprint)) + 1 (tests:2116), then appends a header, each result line as it lands, and a closing line to the sprint's -results.jsonl across the whole suite run (tests:2122-2130, through results_file and appended_line), holding no lock. Trigger: two recorded runs of one test sprint at once, such as two sessions each running 'tests run --sprint <path>' (one with --failing). Both take the same number and their lines interleave. results_rounds then resets rounds[number] at the second header (tests:1949-1951, 'rounds[number] = dict(record, results={}, ...)'), dropping the first run's planned list and tasks_closed, keeps the first result line per scenario from either run (tests:1955, 'rounds[number]["results"].setdefault(record["scenario"], record)'), and takes the closing line of whichever run closed last. Harm (A1, and plumbline-coding rule 3.2, a check-then-write with no lock): the stored record holds a round no complete run produced, and tests failures, stage_fix, complete_failures, and cmd_stamp read it as the latest round. At the base, each round was one line written in one write (base tests:1422), so two concurrent rounds stayed two whole records. Scope: caused by the change (B4/B5, the streamed record). From report i16.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/discover:main. What the code does: review::declared_folders now raises tasks.Unset through tasks.project_config/tasks.setting (review:185, 'folders = tasks.setting(tasks.project_config(root), "folders")') where .ok-planner/config.json is missing, does not parse, or sets no folders; at the base it returned the project root alone. discover::cmd_areas reaches it through review.scoped_files and review.flow_areas (review.tree_files -> project_folders -> declared_folders), but discover::main still catches only (InputError, review.ReviewError) (discover:799). Trigger: 'discover areas' (the /discover-design 'Cut the areas' step) in a project whose config lacks folders or does not parse. Harm (A8): the Unset falls to the __main__ catch-all, which emits DISCOVER.RUN.FAILED {type: Unset} (discover:809-810) for an expected refusal that every sibling tool prints as one '<tool>: <reason>' line. The rule that decides the fix: plumbline-coding rule 1 (a definition changed, every caller site edited in the same change) and the sprint notes' W9 call 'Each tool's owner frame adds tasks.Unset to the refusals it already catches' (sprint notes line 836), which review::main (review:2123) and tests::main (tests:3383) follow. Scope: caused; the raise is new in the change, and discover's catch stood at the base. From report i18.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/discover:cmd_areas. What the code does: discover:165 reads 'budget = (config.get("hunt") or {}).get("area_lines") or 2500', a code default for hunt.area_lines, the setting review::hunt_settings (review:641-645) refuses when missing and .ok-planner/review/config.json declares. Trigger: 'discover areas' (the /discover-design survey step) with a review config holding no hunt, no hunt.area_lines, or area_lines 0: it cuts areas at 2500 lines silently instead of refusing and naming the key. Harm (C1): W9's outcome, 'Every setting in the suite's own scripts ... moves to the project's configuration with no default in code, and a tool that finds one missing refuses and names the key' (realizing decision:settings-have-no-code-defaults), is reached only in part; the notes (line 833) state 'hunt.* ... already refuse when missing'. Scope: the line stood the same at the base, and W9's promised outcome fails through it. From report i21.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/owner-list.md, section 'A stuck defect is a judgment issue', the 'With no issue field' bullet (line 49). What the text does: 'first read issues list --json for an open issue on the same defect; where one stands, file nothing, and use its id as the note below.' Trigger: sprint certification reads no defect issue, so its stuck defects carry no issue field; where the intake already holds an open issue on the same defect (a category: defect issue an earlier /converge filed, or a judgment issue), the owner list files nothing and revises nothing. Harm (C4): the open defect issue keeps category: defect and its generated ruling, so it never reaches the owner as a judgment issue, and the run's fixes tried, verifiers' reasons, and backout result reach the intake nowhere; the next /converge takes it up again as a plain defect. This contradicts decision:intake-writers-are-gated ('each defect stuck at its limit of send-backs, its change backed out of the tree, as a judgment issue'), which W13 realizes and this sprint's delta names, and decision:converge-finds-then-fixes ('the run files it as a judgment issue carrying each fix tried and each verifier's reason'). W13 asked only that a writer check the open issues for a duplicate; the 'With an issue field' bullet beside it (line 48) shows the shape that meets both: revise the open issue into a judgment issue with the '## Stuck in <run>' section. Scope: caused; the change added the file-nothing branch (B401). From report i31.

The story promises: a way to know whether what I approved was delivered, so that done means the same thing for every sprint; the contract's item 2 says the checks pass "or fail only where sprint certification's return lists the failure as a stuck defect", and the goal rule says such a stuck defect holds no term open. Saw, in a scratch project (stack run certify-completion-8ff92de6): a stuck defect filed with only the check's output as its body (tasks item add --pool defects --key gate --state stuck --body "node .ok-planner/bin/plumbline src/late.py: comment-hygiene violation at line 1" -> i2), listed in the return block as "stuck i2: final checks failed on src/late.py"; review certified printed: "item 2 (checks): fails" / "SPRINT NOT COMPLETE" / "- node .ok-planner/bin/plumbline fails on src/late.py, which no stuck defect lists", exit 2. The same tree state with files set on the stuck defect prints SPRINT COMPLETE (verified with stuck i1 site=src/app.py: "item 2 (checks): holds"). So the verdict depends on how a session improvises the unspecified defect, and a sprint the contract calls done is reported not complete.

Reviewed /plan-docs (SKILL.md, core.md, doc-sprint-document.md, _sprint/shared.md blocks, scripts/docs) for bringing every document up to date. The planner, writer, and checker prompts tell each agent to leave a gated element out of reference documentation, and define it only as 'one the code exposes only while an on-off gate setting is on' (core.md lines 113-114 planner, 224 writer, 376 checker); none of the three reads artifact-definitions.md, and none narrows 'gate setting'. The story promises: 'after each update a reader finds documentation that describes the product as it stands'; decision gated-elements-stay-internal limits the term: 'a gate setting is an on-off setting that exists to expose debug or test elements, such as a verb that runs a timed job now' (also skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md:244). Saw: under the prompt's wording, a public verb or route the product exposes behind a user-facing on-off feature setting (not a debug or test gate) reads as gated, so the writer omits it, the checker treats its listing as a false claim of an internal element ('each listed element the intent keeps internal, a gated element among them, is false'), and the reference documentation ships missing a public element a reader relies on. Evidence: core.md:113 'out each gated element, one the code exposes only while an on-off / gate setting is on: it is internal whatever its class, unless an / exception names it.'

Reviewed the declare-to-write chain: /plan-sprint section 5 Docspecs and the DOCSPEC-DEFINITION/TEMPLATE (artifact-definitions.md:162-234) let the owner declare a docspec's ## Notes, 'the owner's standing instructions to the writer: an outline, a passage to keep verbatim, a thing to leave out' (artifact-definitions.md:176). In /plan-docs, the planner and the writer act only through DOC-EDIT-RULES (plan-docs/core.md:7-26), whose rules fire on false claims, listed elements, closed sprints, ## Shape/layout (line 19), and ## Reader/## Covers (line 20); no rule fires on a departure from ## Notes, and line 23 says 'Every other sentence stays as written.' The writer prompt reads ## Notes (line 213) but may edit only where a rule fires. So when the owner adds or amends a Notes instruction on a docspec with existing files (e.g. Notes: 'Keep the sentence "This tool is in beta." verbatim at the top of each file'), docs window reaches the docspec for its own text change, the planner finds no rule that fires on any file, the docspec gets 'No item: nothing its reader sees changed.' (plan-docs/SKILL.md section 5), and the stamp moves forward with the instruction never applied; the same holds for a file that is a change item for another reason. The story promises: 'a way to declare each kind of documentation my project keeps ... so that whoever writes that documentation writes what I asked for'; decision docspec-stamp-opens-the-window takes a docspec 'whose own text ... changed since its stamp'. Saw: only newly written files honor Notes; existing documentation never gets the owner's Notes instructions. Evidence: plan-docs/core.md:19-23 (the rules table and 'Every other sentence stays as written.'); artifact-definitions.md:176.

body: Reviewed the converge skill (SKILL.md, every prompt, the shared blocks, the accept list) and ran its mechanical verbs in a scratch project (stack run find-and-fix-defects-8ff92de6): defects mode end to end (issues file, tasks init, review prompt for every prompt, review backlog, merges --source backlog, snapshot, fixes, verifies, drives --confirm --dry-run, owner-list close as fixed), drive mode with a No stack line (stories, drive-stack, drives, merges --source drive, two sent-back fix rounds, backouts), and analysis mode (areas, hunts --first, merges --round, tally, rotate); every verb behaved as the text says. One gap: a defect issue the backlog takes up whose report the merge rejects for any reason but 'gone' or 'left alone' (merge.md step 2: 'A report whose harm no entry covers is rejected, with the list's reason'; step 1: 'A report whose code does not do what the report says is rejected') is never settled. owner-list.md reads 'the rejected reports with an issue field' but its 'Close the issues the run resolved' section closes only two kinds: 'For every report with an issue field that the merge rejected as gone, close its issue as answered' and 'For every report with an issue field that the merge rejected as left alone, close its issue the same way'. A report rejected as not covered by the accept list gets no close, no revise, and no route, so its issue stays open at route defect; triage skips it as already routed, and every later drive, analysis, or defects run takes it up again through review backlog (BACKLOG_STATES = open, verified), rejects it again, and shows it again as a rejected-report row in the calls table for the owner's veto. The story promises: 'found and fixed without me, so that I meet only the questions that need my judgment'; the cheatsheet's Defect issues section says a defect the run found not real or left standing by the accept list 'closes its issue as answered' with the reason; decision defects-outside-scope-become-defect-issues says a defect issue 'asks the owner for no judgment'. Saw: no sentence in owner-list.md or SKILL.md closes or turns the issue of a backlog report rejected as not covered, so the same rejection returns to the owner every run with nothing ending it.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:read_stream. The select loop that reads the results FIFO runs only while the suite command's stdout pipe is open (tests:1839 'while output is not None:') and ends on stdout EOF (tests:1851 'output = output if data else None'), not on the suite command's exit or the last planned result. After it ends, proc.wait(timeout=max(silence - (time.monotonic() - last), 0)) (tests:1854) waits without reading the FIFO. Trigger A: a suite command whose stdout leaves the pipe early, such as a testing.run ending in '> suite.log' or a wrapper starting 'exec > run.log 2>&1': results landing during the wait never refresh 'last', and once the FIFO buffer fills the writers block; any suite running longer than testing.silence after that is stopped as 'silence', its group killed, and every unread test recorded failed with 'the run stopped after testing.silence seconds with no result'. Trigger B: the suite command exits but a background process it started keeps stdout open: the loop waits a full silence period after the last result and records stopped='silence' over a round in which every test reported, and cmd_run/round_rows print 'the run stopped: no result arrived for testing.silence'. Harm (A3, tests run is a listed operator script; also A9): a correctly configured suite gets passing tests reported failed and a false stop report, and the loop files fix tasks for tests that never failed. Caused: read_stream and run_suite are new in W2. Reports: i10.

Trigger: a test sprint builds a time control control--foo for scenario X (waits "control: control--foo"); tests stamp keeps waits on every scenario (scripts/tests:cmd_stamp l.3186 "for name in ("part", "class", "harm", "waits")", and for a keep, kept = dict(old[...]) carries it forward forever). On the next /plan-tests, X's story is untouched, so assembled_plan adds X as a standing keep copied from the stamp, waits included (l.1276 recorded = {... if name != "issue"}). No planner records a controls item for control--foo, because the product already carries it. Path: SKILL step 8 -> tests plan -> scripts/tests:assembled_plan -> plan_failures -> control_failures l.1169: "elif (waited_control(scenario) or \"\").startswith(CONTROL_PREFIX) and waited_control(scenario) not in ids:" fires for every action, keep included, so assembly refuses "scenario X: it waits on time control control--foo, which no time control item records". The scenario is no planner's item (origins has no entry), so no fix under step 6's "Fixing a planner's items" applies, and every later plan fails to assemble while the stamp records that waits. The sprint's call limits the control:control--<slug> rule to a planned new or rewrite ("A planned new or rewrite names waits ... A control: control--<slug> value must name a control item in the plan"). Scope: caused (control_failures and the waits stamp are new in this change).

C2 under A3 (and A9). Entry: tests run [--sprint] (a script for developers and operators the review facts list) -> cmd_run -> suite_outcome -> run_suite -> read_stream. read_stream's loop runs only while the suite's stdout pipe is open (scripts/tests:1839 'while output is not None:'), and ends it on stdout EOF (l.1849-1851 'output = output if data else None'), not on the suite command's exit or on every planned result landing. Trigger A: the suite command's process closes or replaces the inherited stdout, as a wrapper that starts with 'exec > run.log 2>&1' or a testing.run that ends in '> /dev/null 2>&1' does under sh's exec of a single command. stdout reads EOF at once, the loop ends, and the tool then sits in proc.wait(timeout=max(silence - (now - last), 0)) (l.1853-1856) without reading the FIFO: results that land meanwhile reset no clock, and once the pipe buffer fills the writers block. Any suite that runs longer than testing.silence in total is stopped as 'silence', its process group killed (stop_suite), and every test whose line had not yet been read fails with 'the suite command reported no result; the run stopped after testing.silence seconds with no result' (unreported, l.1897-1904) though results were arriving the whole time. Trigger B (the reverse): the suite command exits but leaves a process that inherited stdout, such as a test stack or server it started in the background. The loop waits the full silence period after the last result, then records stopped='silence' over a round in which every test reported, and cmd_run and round_rows print 'the run stopped: no result arrived for testing.silence' (l.2146-2147, l.2965), which is false, and every round wastes testing.silence seconds. Harm: a correctly configured suite command gets a wrong verdict (tests failed that passed) and a false stop report, and the sprint's loop files fix tasks for tests that never failed. Scope: caused; read_stream and run_suite are new in this change (W2).

C1, W5 (and the I-less W5 call: 'On accept, the verifier sends each named test back (W1 path)'). Entry: test sprint step 6 -> tests run --sprint (a round whose testing.leftovers count grew) -> tests failures lists leftovers--<kind> -> tests tasks --stage fix (stage_fix) -> fixer records change=none with tests=[<scenario>] -> verify task -> core.md {{TEST-VERIFY-PROMPT}} 'A grown leftover count': 'On accepting it, send each test it names back to a test task: tasks item set <that scenario's latest item in the tests pool> --state sent-back'. Where it ends: when the named scenario's test was not written in this test sprint (action keep, or adopt from a legacy suite), no test task ran for it, so the tests pool holds no item for it and the verifier has nothing to send back. sent_back_tests/refiled_tests (scripts/tests:2341-2377) refile only from a tests item in state sent-back, and stage_write files a test task only for actions in WRITTEN (new, rewrite, retire; l.2558-2559), so no test task is ever filed for that scenario. unrewritten_tests (l.2978-2993) then requires 'a test task with key <named> closed done after the accepting verify task' and complete_failures appends 'fixes item ..., accepted, names test <sid> as leaving the resource behind, and no test task rewrote it' on every call: TESTS COMPLETE can never print, and the gate round grows the same count again, so step 6 (no cap) refiles the same leftovers fix. Outcome not reached: W5's 'a count that grew fails the round' has no route to a passing run when a kept or adopted test leaks, which is the likeliest leaker since no earlier sprint measured leftovers. body: Entry point: the edit hook, scripts/hooks/post-edit.js:57-58, calls plumbline's findProjectRoot and then inProject(root, target). findProjectRoot (plumbline:733-740) also calls inProject for a file that has no .ok-planner ancestor. inProject (plumbline:686-690) asks declaredFolders (plumbline:677-684) for the folders the project owns outside its root. Where it ends: declaredFolders still defaults the setting. `if (!fs.existsSync(configPath)) return [];` and `if (read.userConfig === null || !('folders' in read.userConfig)) return [];` read a missing .ok-planner/config.json, or one that sets no folders, as 'the estate root alone'. They do not refuse and name the key. Outcome: W9 says 'a tool that finds one missing refuses and names the key'. The amended decision project-declares-its-folders says the list has 'no default', and 'Every tool that lists or scopes the project's code reads that list: ... the lint and its edit hook'. W9 removed this default from loadConfig (unsetLintKeys) and from review::declared_folders, but it left it in the lint's other folders reader. B7 (rewrite; B2 rewrite across Trued-up projects). User left behind: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review::declared_folders, in the release, and through review::project_folders every tool that lists the project's folders (review changed/areas/checks/snapshot/certified, tests window/groups/plan/run/stray/complete, docs window). C2 under A3 (an operator script gives a wrong result; also A9: the round reports failures that did not happen). Trigger: a suite command whose own stdout leaves the tool's pipe before the suite ends, such as testing.run = 'node scripts/suite.mjs {tests} {results} > suite.log' (the shell execs the single command with its redirect, so the pipe's write end closes at once), or a runner that daemonizes its workers. brief:
fix round 1; defects i38 i50 i54 i55
- i38: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:cmd_run. What the code does: a recorded run reads the round number from a plain read, number = len(results_rounds(root, sprint)) + 1 (tests:2116), then appends a header, each result line as it lands, and a closing line to the sprint's -results.jsonl across the whole suite run (tests:2122-2130, through results_file and appended_line), holding no lock. Trigger: two recorded runs of one test sprint at once, such as two sessions each running 'tests run --sprint <path>' (one with --failing). Both take the same number and their lines interleave. results_rounds then resets rounds[number] at the second header (tests:1949-1951, 'rounds[number] = dict(record, results={}, ...)'), dropping the first run's planned list and tasks_closed, keeps the first result line per scenario from either run (tests:1955, 'rounds[number]["results"].setdefault(record["scenario"], record)'), and takes the closing line of whichever run closed last. Harm (A1, and plumbline-coding rule 3.2, a check-then-write with no lock): the stored record holds a round no complete run produced, and tests failures, stage_fix, complete_failures, and cmd_stamp read it as the latest round. At the base, each round was one line written in one write (base tests:1422), so two concurrent rounds stayed two whole records. Scope: caused by the change (B4/B5, the streamed record). From report i16.
- i50: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:read_stream. The select loop that reads the results FIFO runs only while the suite command's stdout pipe is open (tests:1839 'while output is not None:') and ends on stdout EOF (tests:1851 'output = output if data else None'), not on the suite command's exit or the last planned result. After it ends, proc.wait(timeout=max(silence - (time.monotonic() - last), 0)) (tests:1854) waits without reading the FIFO. Trigger A: a suite command whose stdout leaves the pipe early, such as a testing.run ending in '> suite.log' or a wrapper starting 'exec > run.log 2>&1': results landing during the wait never refresh 'last', and once the FIFO buffer fills the writers block; any suite running longer than testing.silence after that is stopped as 'silence', its group killed, and every unread test recorded failed with 'the run stopped after testing.silence seconds with no result'. Trigger B: the suite command exits but a background process it started keeps stdout open: the loop waits a full silence period after the last result and records stopped='silence' over a round in which every test reported, and cmd_run/round_rows print 'the run stopped: no result arrived for testing.silence'. Harm (A3, tests run is a listed operator script; also A9): a correctly configured suite gets passing tests reported failed and a false stop report, and the loop files fix tasks for tests that never failed. Caused: read_stream and run_suite are new in W2. Reports: i10.
- i54: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:control_failures. tests stamp records waits on every scenario (tests:3186 'for name in ("part", "class", "harm", "waits")') and a keep carries the old record forward (kept = dict(old[...])). On a later /plan-tests whose run leaves the story untouched, assembled_plan adds the scenario as a standing keep copied from the stamp, waits included (tests:1276 'recorded = {name: value for name, value in old_by_id[sid].items() if name != "issue"}'), while the plan's controls come only from planners' controls items, and no planner records one for a control the product already carries. control_failures then checks every action, keep included (tests:1169 'elif (waited_control(scenario) or "").startswith(CONTROL_PREFIX) and waited_control(scenario) not in ids:'), and assembly refuses 'scenario X: it waits on time control control--foo, which no time control item records'. The scenario rests on no planner's item, so no fix under step 6's 'Fixing a planner's items' applies. Trigger: any test sprint built a time control and its waiting scenario stands. Harm (A3, /plan-tests is public surface): /plan-tests can never assemble a plan again while the stamp records that waits. The sprint's call limits the control rule to a planned new or rewrite. Caused: control_failures and the waits stamp are new (W4). Reports: i9.
- i55: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:unrewritten_tests, with refiled_tests/sent_back_tests and core.md's verify prompt 'A grown leftover count'. On accepting a change=none leftovers fix, the verifier is told to 'send each test it names back to a test task: tasks item set <that scenario's latest item in the tests pool> --state sent-back' (core.md:1557-1561). A kept or adopted test has no item in the tests pool: only test tasks (core.md:1258) and the sweep (core.md:1357) add one, and stage_write files test tasks only for actions in WRITTEN ('new', 'rewrite', 'retire'; tests:2558). sent_back_tests/refiled_tests (tests:2341-2377) refile only from a tests item in state sent-back. unrewritten_tests (tests:2978-2993) requires 'a test task with key <named> closed done after the accepting verify task', so complete_failures reports 'fixes item ..., accepted, names test <sid> as leaving the resource behind, and no test task rewrote it' on every call. body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-docs/core.md, the planner (lines 112-114), writer (lines 223-226, 240-241), and checker (lines 375-380) prompts, added by W11. What the text does: each tells its agent to leave out a gated element and defines it only as 'one the code exposes only while an on-off gate setting is on'; none says what a gate setting is, and none of the three agents reads artifact-definitions.md. Decision gated-elements-stay-internal (a delta of this sprint) bounds the term: 'a gate setting is an on-off setting that exists to expose debug or test elements, such as a verb that runs a timed job now or an admin route that moves the product's clock' (also skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md:244). Trigger: a docspec with ## Lists over a class whose public member the product exposes behind a user-facing on-off feature setting. Harm (C4, decision gated-elements-stay-internal contradicted; story keep-documentation-current): the writer reads that member as gated and omits it, and the checker counts its listing as false ('each listed element the intent keeps internal, a gated element among them, is false'), so the reference documentation ships without a public element its reader relies on. W11 asked for these lines. The same unbounded wording stands in the other readers W11 changed: plan-sprint/core.md:348-349 (code planner step 9), plan-sprint/SKILL.md:122 (the surface), converge/prompts/hunt-flow.md:9 and converge/SKILL.md:14, 89 (flow areas), scripts/ok-planner-cheatsheet.md:298-299, scripts/ok-planner-CLAUDE.md:159-161. Evidence: core.md:113-114 'out each gated element, one the code exposes only while an on-off / gate setting is on: it is internal whatever its class, unless an / exception names it.' Drive failure i37 (driver t25).
note: Bounded the gate setting at every site W11 changed to the decision gated-elements-stay-internal wording, 'a gate setting is on, an on-off setting that exists to expose debug or test elements': plan-docs/core.md planner (113-114), writer (224-226), checker (376-378); plan-sprint/core.md step 10; plan-sprint/SKILL.md The surface; converge/prompts/hunt-flow.md Trace; converge/SKILL.md lines 14 and 89; scripts/ok-planner-cheatsheet.md The public surface; scripts/ok-planner-CLAUDE.md surface paragraph. A user-facing on-off feature setting no longer reads as a gate, so its public members are listed and not counted false. rg 'on-off gate' leaves only the time-control rules in docs/plumbline-coding.md and docs/plumbline-cheatsheet.md, which name test controls and fit the bound.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:declared_folders (B7, rewrite). B7 made plumbline::testingDefects report the earlier one-test testing form (plumbline:332 'testing declares the earlier one-test form; run /ok, ...'), and lists only admin/true-up as its user in the release. review::declared_folders is also a user: it runs config-check and reads the project root alone on any defect (review:193-196 'if ran.returncode == 2 and defects: return [], ("%s is malformed, so %s reads the project root alone ...'). Its goal, from decision project-declares-its-folders and the W9 call 'the review's use of config-check for folders, which must not switch to "root alone" because an unrelated key is absent': read the declared folders unless folders itself is malformed. After: config-check exits 2 on the testing line, and review changed, areas, checks, snapshot, and certified, and the tests verbs through project_folders, drop every file under the declared folders; B2's ruling accepts only that bin/tests and config-check refuse the earlier form. R3: a rewrite left a user in the release behind. Caused. Reports: i14.
note: scripts/review declared_folders now reads only config-check lines about folders (lines starting 'folders ' or 'folders[', the forms plumbline foldersDefects/folderDefect print) and falls back to the project root alone only where one stands, naming just those lines; a defect in another key, such as the earlier one-test testing form, leaves exit 2 with no folders line, so it returns config.folders as before B7. Parse-level defects cannot reach config-check here because tasks.project_config already parsed the file. Callers project_folders and cmd_certified take the same return shape. Files: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:cmd_run. What the code does: a recorded run reads the round number from a plain read, number = len(results_rounds(root, sprint)) + 1 (tests:2116), then appends a header, each result line as it lands, and a closing line to the sprint's -results.jsonl across the whole suite run (tests:2122-2130, through results_file and appended_line), holding no lock. Trigger: two recorded runs of one test sprint at once, such as two sessions each running 'tests run --sprint <path>' (one with --failing). Both take the same number and their lines interleave. results_rounds then resets rounds[number] at the second header (tests:1949-1951, 'rounds[number] = dict(record, results={}, ...)'), dropping the first run's planned list and tasks_closed, keeps the first result line per scenario from either run (tests:1955, 'rounds[number]["results"].setdefault(record["scenario"], record)'), and takes the closing line of whichever run closed last. Harm (A1, and plumbline-coding rule 3.2, a check-then-write with no lock): the stored record holds a round no complete run produced, and tests failures, stage_fix, complete_failures, and cmd_stamp read it as the latest round. At the base, each round was one line written in one write (base tests:1422), so two concurrent rounds stayed two whole records. Scope: caused by the change (B4/B5, the streamed record). From report i16.
note: scripts/tests: cmd_run now takes round_lock (an exclusive non-blocking flock on .ok-planner/.cache/tests-<sprint>.lock) around the whole recorded run, moved into tested_round: the target list, the round number from results_rounds, the header, every result line, and the closing line are all read and written under the lock. A second recorded run of the same test sprint refuses at once with a message naming the run under way and the results file, so two rounds can no longer take one number or interleave. Usage text of tests run says so. Unrecorded runs (--only, --from) take no lock. Files: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:read_stream. The select loop that reads the results FIFO runs only while the suite command's stdout pipe is open (tests:1839 'while output is not None:') and ends on stdout EOF (tests:1851 'output = output if data else None'), not on the suite command's exit or the last planned result. After it ends, proc.wait(timeout=max(silence - (time.monotonic() - last), 0)) (tests:1854) waits without reading the FIFO. Trigger A: a suite command whose stdout leaves the pipe early, such as a testing.run ending in '> suite.log' or a wrapper starting 'exec > run.log 2>&1': results landing during the wait never refresh 'last', and once the FIFO buffer fills the writers block; any suite running longer than testing.silence after that is stopped as 'silence', its group killed, and every unread test recorded failed with 'the run stopped after testing.silence seconds with no result'. Trigger B: the suite command exits but a background process it started keeps stdout open: the loop waits a full silence period after the last result and records stopped='silence' over a round in which every test reported, and cmd_run/round_rows print 'the run stopped: no result arrived for testing.silence'. Harm (A3, tests run is a listed operator script; also A9): a correctly configured suite gets passing tests reported failed and a false stop report, and the loop files fix tasks for tests that never failed. Caused: read_stream and run_suite are new in W2. Reports: i10.
note: scripts/tests: read_stream now loops on the suite command's exit, not its stdout EOF. exit_watch starts a daemon thread that waits on the process and closes the write end of a pipe; the loop selects on the results FIFO, stdout (dropped from the watch at EOF), and that pipe, refreshing last on each result, and ends when the process exits or testing.silence passes with no result. The old proc.wait(timeout) that read no FIFO is gone. Trigger A (stdout redirected away) keeps reading results; trigger B (a background child holding stdout) ends at the command's exit. run_suite closes the pipe end in its cleanup. Shared between threads: proc alone, whose waits Popen guards with its own waitpid lock; the thread alone owns and closes its pipe end. Probed with throwaway suite commands: redirected stdout 2.0s no stop; held stdout 0.0s no stop; real silence stops. Files: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:control_failures. tests stamp records waits on every scenario (tests:3186 'for name in ("part", "class", "harm", "waits")') and a keep carries the old record forward (kept = dict(old[...])). On a later /plan-tests whose run leaves the story untouched, assembled_plan adds the scenario as a standing keep copied from the stamp, waits included (tests:1276 'recorded = {name: value for name, value in old_by_id[sid].items() if name != "issue"}'), while the plan's controls come only from planners' controls items, and no planner records one for a control the product already carries. control_failures then checks every action, keep included (tests:1169 'elif (waited_control(scenario) or "").startswith(CONTROL_PREFIX) and waited_control(scenario) not in ids:'), and assembly refuses 'scenario X: it waits on time control control--foo, which no time control item records'. The scenario rests on no planner's item, so no fix under step 6's 'Fixing a planner's items' applies. Trigger: any test sprint built a time control and its waiting scenario stands. Harm (A3, /plan-tests is public surface): /plan-tests can never assemble a plan again while the stamp records that waits. The sprint's call limits the control rule to a planned new or rewrite. Caused: control_failures and the waits stamp are new (W4). Reports: i9.
note: scripts/tests: control_failures checks that a waited control--<slug> has a time control item only for a new or rewritten scenario, as the sprint's call limits the rule; a keep carried from the stamp with its waits no longer refuses assembly. Usage text of tests plan says so. Files: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:unrewritten_tests, with refiled_tests/sent_back_tests and core.md's verify prompt 'A grown leftover count'. On accepting a change=none leftovers fix, the verifier is told to 'send each test it names back to a test task: tasks item set <that scenario's latest item in the tests pool> --state sent-back' (core.md:1557-1561). A kept or adopted test has no item in the tests pool: only test tasks (core.md:1258) and the sweep (core.md:1357) add one, and stage_write files test tasks only for actions in WRITTEN ('new', 'rewrite', 'retire'; tests:2558). sent_back_tests/refiled_tests (tests:2341-2377) refile only from a tests item in state sent-back. unrewritten_tests (tests:2978-2993) requires 'a test task with key <named> closed done after the accepting verify task', so complete_failures reports 'fixes item ..., accepted, names test <sid> as leaving the resource behind, and no test task rewrote it' on every call. Trigger: a round's testing.leftovers count grows and the leaking test is a kept or adopted one, the likeliest leaker since no earlier sprint measured leftovers. Outcome not reached (W5, 'a count that grew fails the round', and its call that the verifier sends each named test back on the W1 path): TESTS COMPLETE can never print, the gate round grows the count again, and the uncapped loop refiles the same fix; the W1 fix-verifier send-back fails through the same site for a kept or adopted test. Caused: the leftovers path, unrewritten_tests, and the send-back text are new. Reports: i11.
note: skills/plan-tests/core.md: the verify prompt gains 'Send a test back', which both send-back sites (the fix whose test waits on elapsed time, and an accepted change=none leftovers item) now use: set the scenario's latest tests item sent-back, or where the pool holds none, as for a kept or adopted test, add a tests item with scenario, path, name, and state sent-back. refiled_tests already files a fresh test task from a sent-back item with no earlier test task, so the test is rewritten and unrewritten_tests finds a test task closed done after the accepting verify. The write prompt reads the test as it stands for a sent-back test and rewrites it whatever action the brief names. Files: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-tests/core.md.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:cmd_run. What the code does: a recorded run reads the round number from a plain read, number = len(results_rounds(root, sprint)) + 1 (tests:2116), then appends a header, each result line as it lands, and a closing line to the sprint's -results.jsonl across the whole suite run (tests:2122-2130, through results_file and appended_line), holding no lock. Trigger: two recorded runs of one test sprint at once, such as two sessions each running 'tests run --sprint <path>' (one with --failing). Both take the same number and their lines interleave. results_rounds then resets rounds[number] at the second header (tests:1949-1951, 'rounds[number] = dict(record, results={}, ...)'), dropping the first run's planned list and tasks_closed, keeps the first result line per scenario from either run (tests:1955, 'rounds[number]["results"].setdefault(record["scenario"], record)'), and takes the closing line of whichever run closed last. Harm (A1, and plumbline-coding rule 3.2, a check-then-write with no lock): the stored record holds a round no complete run produced, and tests failures, stage_fix, complete_failures, and cmd_stamp read it as the latest round. At the base, each round was one line written in one write (base tests:1422), so two concurrent rounds stayed two whole records. Scope: caused by the change (B4/B5, the streamed record). From report i16.
note: t81: cmd_run wraps tested_round in round_lock (non-blocking flock on .cache/tests-<sprint>.lock) for recorded runs; round number read, header, result lines, and closing line all under it; second recorded run refuses with InputError through main's owner frame (exit 1, actionable message). Probed two processes: second refused, reacquired after release. Lint clean.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:read_stream. The select loop that reads the results FIFO runs only while the suite command's stdout pipe is open (tests:1839 'while output is not None:') and ends on stdout EOF (tests:1851 'output = output if data else None'), not on the suite command's exit or the last planned result. After it ends, proc.wait(timeout=max(silence - (time.monotonic() - last), 0)) (tests:1854) waits without reading the FIFO. Trigger A: a suite command whose stdout leaves the pipe early, such as a testing.run ending in '> suite.log' or a wrapper starting 'exec > run.log 2>&1': results landing during the wait never refresh 'last', and once the FIFO buffer fills the writers block; any suite running longer than testing.silence after that is stopped as 'silence', its group killed, and every unread test recorded failed with 'the run stopped after testing.silence seconds with no result'. Trigger B: the suite command exits but a background process it started keeps stdout open: the loop waits a full silence period after the last result and records stopped='silence' over a round in which every test reported, and cmd_run/round_rows print 'the run stopped: no result arrived for testing.silence'. Harm (A3, tests run is a listed operator script; also A9): a correctly configured suite gets passing tests reported failed and a false stop report, and the loop files fix tasks for tests that never failed. Caused: read_stream and run_suite are new in W2. Reports: i10.
note: t81: read_stream loops on an exit-watch pipe closed by a daemon thread after proc.wait, selecting FIFO, stdout (dropped at EOF), waker; old proc.wait(timeout) without FIFO reads removed; final stream_lines drains FIFO (holder keeps a write end, so no EOF spin); poll after waker sees returncode set. Thread body catches Exception, emits TESTS.SUITE.UNWATCHED, closes its end in finally; stop_suite's wait coexists via Popen waitpid lock. Probed: stdout redirected 4.0s with 1.5s gaps under silence 2, both results, no stop; held stdout 0.0s, no stop; real silence stops at 2s. Lint clean.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:control_failures. tests stamp records waits on every scenario (tests:3186 'for name in ("part", "class", "harm", "waits")') and a keep carries the old record forward (kept = dict(old[...])). On a later /plan-tests whose run leaves the story untouched, assembled_plan adds the scenario as a standing keep copied from the stamp, waits included (tests:1276 'recorded = {name: value for name, value in old_by_id[sid].items() if name != "issue"}'), while the plan's controls come only from planners' controls items, and no planner records one for a control the product already carries. control_failures then checks every action, keep included (tests:1169 'elif (waited_control(scenario) or "").startswith(CONTROL_PREFIX) and waited_control(scenario) not in ids:'), and assembly refuses 'scenario X: it waits on time control control--foo, which no time control item records'. The scenario rests on no planner's item, so no fix under step 6's 'Fixing a planner's items' applies. Trigger: any test sprint built a time control and its waiting scenario stands. Harm (A3, /plan-tests is public surface): /plan-tests can never assemble a plan again while the stamp records that waits. The sprint's call limits the control rule to a planned new or rewrite. Caused: control_failures and the waits stamp are new (W4). Reports: i9.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:unrewritten_tests, with refiled_tests/sent_back_tests and core.md's verify prompt 'A grown leftover count'. On accepting a change=none leftovers fix, the verifier is told to 'send each test it names back to a test task: tasks item set <that scenario's latest item in the tests pool> --state sent-back' (core.md:1557-1561). A kept or adopted test has no item in the tests pool: only test tasks (core.md:1258) and the sweep (core.md:1357) add one, and stage_write files test tasks only for actions in WRITTEN ('new', 'rewrite', 'retire'; tests:2558). sent_back_tests/refiled_tests (tests:2341-2377) refile only from a tests item in state sent-back. unrewritten_tests (tests:2978-2993) requires 'a test task with key <named> closed done after the accepting verify task', so complete_failures reports 'fixes item ..., accepted, names test <sid> as leaving the resource behind, and no test task rewrote it' on every call. Trigger: a round's testing.leftovers count grows and the leaking test is a kept or adopted one, the likeliest leaker since no earlier sprint measured leftovers. Outcome not reached (W5, 'a count that grew fails the round', and its call that the verifier sends each named test back on the W1 path): TESTS COMPLETE can never print, the gate round grows the count again, and the uncapped loop refiles the same fix; the W1 fix-verifier send-back fails through the same site for a kept or adopted test. Caused: the leftovers path, unrewritten_tests, and the send-back text are new. Reports: i11.
note: t81: core.md verify prompt adds 'Send a test back', used by the elapsed-time and change=none leftovers sites: set the latest tests item sent-back or, where none, add one with scenario/path/name, state sent-back (allowed by the tests pool item_states). recorded_tests keys by scenario field; sent_back_tests/refiled_tests file a fresh test task with key=scenario, files=path, and brief 'The verifier sent the test back: <reason>', which the write prompt now reads and rewrites whatever the action; that task closing done after the verify satisfies unrewritten_tests. body: Reviewed the declare-to-write chain: /plan-sprint section 5 Docspecs and the DOCSPEC-DEFINITION/TEMPLATE (artifact-definitions.md:162-234) let the owner declare a docspec's ## Notes, 'the owner's standing instructions to the writer: an outline, a passage to keep verbatim, a thing to leave out' (artifact-definitions.md:176). In /plan-docs, the planner and the writer act only through DOC-EDIT-RULES (plan-docs/core.md:7-26), whose rules fire on false claims, listed elements, closed sprints, ## Shape/layout (line 19), and ## Reader/## Covers (line 20); no rule fires on a departure from ## Notes, and line 23 says 'Every other sentence stays as written.' The writer prompt reads ## Notes (line 213) but may edit only where a rule fires. So when the owner adds or amends a Notes instruction on a docspec with existing files (e.g. Notes: 'Keep the sentence "This tool is in beta." verbatim at the top of each file'), docs window reaches the docspec for its own text change, the planner finds no rule that fires on any file, the docspec gets 'No item: nothing its reader sees changed.' (plan-docs/SKILL.md section 5), and the stamp moves forward with the instruction never applied; the same holds for a file that is a change item for another reason. The story promises: 'a way to declare each kind of documentation my project keeps ... so that whoever writes that documentation writes what I asked for'; decision docspec-stamp-opens-the-window takes a docspec 'whose own text ... changed since its stamp'. Saw: only newly written files honor Notes; existing documentation never gets the owner's Notes instructions. Evidence: plan-docs/core.md:19-23 (the rules table and 'Every other sentence stays as written.'); artifact-definitions.md:176.
note: doc-edit-rules-ignore-docspec-notes

body: Reviewed the style pass, DOC-STYLE-PROMPT (plan-docs/core.md:277-337). It reads the docspec whole, then 'revise it against the docspec's ## Shape and layout, the worked example, and the writing standard' (line 314), and its limit is only 'keep every claim's meaning, add no claim, and cut none' (line 323). It is never told to keep what the docspec's ## Notes orders, so a passage the owner's Notes says to keep verbatim (artifact-definitions.md:176: 'a passage to keep verbatim') may be reworded by the style pass under the writing standard (shortest word, active voice), and an outline Notes gives may be reordered to the worked example's order. The story promises: 'so that whoever writes that documentation writes what I asked for'. Saw: the cold style pass, which edits every reviewed file, takes the shape, example, and standard as its only authorities and can undo the Notes instructions the writer followed. Evidence: plan-docs/core.md:314-325.
note: doc-style-pass-may-undo-docspec-notes

body: Reviewed the converge skill (SKILL.md, every prompt, the shared blocks, the accept list) and ran its mechanical verbs in a scratch project (stack run find-and-fix-defects-8ff92de6): defects mode end to end (issues file, tasks init, review prompt for every prompt, review backlog, merges --source backlog, snapshot, fixes, verifies, drives --confirm --dry-run, owner-list close as fixed), drive mode with a No stack line (stories, drive-stack, drives, merges --source drive, two sent-back fix rounds, backouts), and analysis mode (areas, hunts --first, merges --round, tally, rotate); every verb behaved as the text says. One gap: a defect issue the backlog takes up whose report the merge rejects for any reason but 'gone' or 'left alone' (merge.md step 2: 'A report whose harm no entry covers is rejected, with the list's reason'; step 1: 'A report whose code does not do what the report says is rejected') is never settled. owner-list.md reads 'the rejected reports with an issue field' but its 'Close the issues the run resolved' section closes only two kinds: 'For every report with an issue field that the merge rejected as gone, close its issue as answered' and 'For every report with an issue field that the merge rejected as left alone, close its issue the same way'. A report rejected as not covered by the accept list gets no close, no revise, and no route, so its issue stays open at route defect; triage skips it as already routed, and every later drive, analysis, or defects run takes it up again through review backlog (BACKLOG_STATES = open, verified), rejects it again, and shows it again as a rejected-report row in the calls table for the owner's veto. The story promises: 'found and fixed without me, so that I meet only the questions that need my judgment'; the cheatsheet's Defect issues section says a defect the run found not real or left standing by the accept list 'closes its issue as answered' with the reason; decision defects-outside-scope-become-defect-issues says a defect issue 'asks the owner for no judgment'. Saw: no sentence in owner-list.md or SKILL.md closes or turns the issue of a backlog report rejected as not covered, so the same rejection returns to the owner every run with nothing ending it.
note: owner-list-leaves-rejected-backlog-issues-open
